derivations.title: Dimensional relation for the period of a simple pendulum
derivations.starting_relationship: Assume T = k lˣ gʸ mᶻ
derivations.final_result: Assume T = k lˣ gʸ mᶻ; equating dimensions gives x+y=0, −2y=1, z=0, hence T=k√(l/g).

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: T = k lˣ gʸ mᶻ; [L⁰M⁰T]=[Lˣ][LT⁻²]ʸ[M]ᶻ; x+y=0, −2y=1, z=0; so T=k l½g⁻½ = k√(l/g).

derivations.title: Uniform-acceleration displacement from velocity-time graph
derivations.starting_relationship: v=v_0+at, area under the velocity-time graph equals displacement
derivations.final_result: Starting from v=v₀+at; graph area gives x=½(v−v₀)t+v₀t, hence x=x₀+v₀t+½at².

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: Area under v-t curve = triangle ABC + rectangle OACD; x=½(v−v₀)t+v₀t; using v−v₀=at gives x=x₀+v₀t+½at². Mathematical progression: Starting from v=v₀+at; graph area gives x=½(v−v₀)t+v₀t, hence x=x₀+v₀t+½at².

derivations.title: Velocity-displacement equation
derivations.final_result: Substitute t=(v−v₀)/a into x=(v₀+v)t/2 to obtain v²=v₀²+2a(x−x₀).

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: From Eq. (2.4), t=(v−v₀)/a. Substituting this in Eq. (2.7a) ... v²−v₀²=2ax; generalized as 2a(x−x₀). Mathematical progression: Substitute t=(v−v₀)/a into x=(v₀+v)t/2 to obtain v²=v₀²+2a(x−x₀).

derivations.title: Kinematic equations by calculus
derivations.final_result: Integrate dv=a dt, dx=v dt and v dv=a dx for constant a to obtain the three constant-acceleration equations.

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: By definition dv/dt=a ... Integrating ... v=v₀+at; further dx/dt=v ... x=x₀+v₀t+½at²; v dv=a dx ... v²−v₀²=2a(x−x₀). Mathematical progression: Integrate dv=a dt, dx=v dt and v dv=a dx for constant a to obtain the three constant-acceleration equations.

derivations.title: Free-fall equations
derivations.starting_relationship: a=-g and v_0=0 in the kinematic equations
derivations.final_result: Substitute a=−g and v₀=0 into constant-acceleration equations to express velocity, position and velocity-squared for an object released from rest.

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: v=0−gt; y=0−½gt²; v²=0−2gy. Mathematical progression: Substitute a=−g and v₀=0 into constant-acceleration equations to express velocity, position and velocity-squared for an object released from rest.

derivations.title: Galileo’s odd-number distance sequence
derivations.final_result: Using y=−½gt² at successive equal times τ, 2τ, 3τ,… gives successive distances proportional to 1,3,5,7,…

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: positions ... 0, τ, 2τ, 3τ ...; the distances traversed in successive τs ... ratio 1:3:5:7:9:11 Mathematical progression: Using y=−½gt² at successive equal times τ, 2τ, 3τ,… gives successive distances proportional to 1,3,5,7,…

derivations.title: Stopping distance under constant deceleration
derivations.final_result: Set final velocity v=0 in v²=v₀²+2ad to obtain dₛ=−v₀²/(2a), for braking acceleration a<0.

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: using equation of motion v²=v₀²+2ax, and noting that v=0, we have the stopping distance Mathematical progression: Set final velocity v=0 in v²=v₀²+2ad to obtain dₛ=−v₀²/(2a), for braking acceleration a<0.

derivations.title: Vector resultant by parallelogram geometry
derivations.starting_relationship: R=A+B; resolve along the parallelogram geometry
derivations.final_result: Resolve R into components; geometry gives R²=A²+B²+2AB cosθ and direction through the sine rule.

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: OS²=ON²+SN²; ON=A+B cosθ; SN=B sinθ; hence R²=A²+B²+2AB cosθ; then derive sine relations for direction. Progressive equations and geometric steps summarized in final_result.

derivations.title: Component addition of vectors
derivations.starting_relationship: A=A_x\\hat i+A_y\\hat j; B=B_x\\hat i+B_y\\hat j
derivations.final_result: Write A and B in unit-vector components and regroup to obtain Rₓ=Aₓ+Bₓ and Rᵧ=Aᵧ+Bᵧ.

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: R=A+B=(Aₓ+Bₓ)i+(Aᵧ+Bᵧ)j; so Rₓ=Aₓ+Bₓ, Rᵧ=Aᵧ+Bᵧ. Progressive equations and geometric steps summarized in final_result.

derivations.title: Constant-acceleration position in a plane
derivations.starting_relationship: \\mathbf v=\\mathbf v_0+\\mathbf a t; \\Delta\\mathbf r=\\frac{\\mathbf v_0+\\mathbf v}{2}t
derivations.final_result: Use v=v₀+at and displacement=(v₀+v)t/2 to derive r=r₀+v₀t+½at².

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: average velocity is (v₀+v)/2; displacement ...; r−r₀=v₀t+½at². Progressive equations and geometric steps summarized in final_result.

derivations.title: Projectile trajectory and range relations
derivations.final_result: Resolve initial velocity, use x=v₀cosθ₀ t and y=v₀sinθ₀ t−½gt², eliminate t for the parabolic path; derive flight time, height, range.

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: eliminating time ... y=(tanθ₀)x−g x²/(2v₀²cos²θ₀); then derive tₘ, T_f, hₘ, R from component equations. Progressive equations and geometric steps summarized in final_result.

derivations.title: Centripetal acceleration
derivations.final_result: Similar position/velocity triangles yield Δv/v=Δr/R; as Δt→0 and Δr/Δt→v, a_c=v²/R directed to centre.

source_location.book: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XI

derivations.evidence: triangles ... are similar ... Δv/v=Δr/R; if Δt is small ... Δr/Δt≈v; therefore centripetal acceleration. Progressive equations and geometric steps summarized in final_result.
